To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
career training and overeducation both have positive effects on upward mobility, and that these effects do not only hold for the primary labour market but also for the supplementary labour market.

(a) overeducated workers have a higher upward mobility than workers with the right educational qualifications for their jobs; (b) career training has a positive effect on upward mobility, but this is especially the case in the supplementary segment; and (c) the supplementary labour market plays an important role as an intermediary segment in the transition process from initial education to the labour market.
